data: European Space Agency (Mercury Planetary Orbiter + Mercury Transfer Module) / Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, Mio)

4100 kg launch stack: MTM (Mercury Transfer Module, ESA — 4 ion thrusters, solar arrays) + MPO (Mercury Planetary Orbiter, ESA, 1230 kg, 11 instruments) + MIO (Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, JAXA, 255 kg, 5 instruments) + MOSIF sunshield. Two science orbiters separate after Mercury arrival.

© ESA / JAXA / Airbus. BepiColombo launched 2018-10-20 from Kourou — the joint Europe-Japan flagship to Mercury, named after Giuseppe (Bepi) Colombo, the Italian mathematician who designed Mariner 10's multi-flyby trajectory. The 8-year cruise uses 9 gravity assists (Earth 2020-04-10, Venus 2020-10-15, Venus 2021-08-10, then six Mercury flybys 2021–2025) plus continuous ion-electric thrust from the Mercury Transfer Module to bleed off the enormous solar-gravity gradient between Earth and Mercury orbits. Mercury orbit insertion is set for 2026-11-21, with science operations beginning early 2027 after MTM jettison and MPO + Mio separation. Primary science: Mercury's exospheric composition + dynamics, the composition of its iron-rich crust and Caloris-class large impact basins, the structure of its magnetic field + magnetospheric tail, and tests of Einstein's general relativity via radio-science range tracking through Mercury's strong solar-gravity environment. Nominal one-year mission with one-year extension authorised.

Kourou, French Guiana, 2018-10-20. Joint ESA / JAXA mission carrying two science orbiters — ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter (MPO) + JAXA's Mio (formerly Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter) — stacked on a Mercury Transfer Module that uses electric propulsion + nine planetary flybys to lose enough energy to capture into Mercury orbit.

Closest approach 12,700 km on 2020-04-10. The first of nine flybys needed to lose orbital energy and spiral inward toward Mercury. Reaching Mercury directly from Earth is among the hardest interplanetary transfers — falling toward the Sun the spacecraft speeds up (Mercury orbits at about 47 km/s, Earth at about 30), so it has to shed a great deal of orbital energy to be slow enough relative to Mercury to be captured — the opposite of an outer-system mission's accelerate-and-go problem.

Closest approach 10,720 km on 2020-10-15. First of two Venus assists. Venus's gravity is used here to BRAKE the spacecraft — taking energy out of the heliocentric orbit so the perihelion drops toward Mercury's distance from the Sun.
Closest approach 552 km on 2021-08-10 — much closer than Venus #1. The deeper flyby drops aphelion further, setting up the first of six Mercury flybys 11 months later.

Closest approach 199 km from Mercury's surface on 2021-10-01 — the first BepiColombo Mercury observation, four years before formal orbit insertion. Each successive Mercury flyby brakes the spacecraft further, shrinking its orbit closer to Mercury's.

Closest approach 200 km on 2022-06-23. Cumulative ∆v from gravity assists exceeds 6 km/s by this pass — work the chemical engine + electric thrusters can't have done alone within the propellant budget.
Closest approach 236 km on 2023-06-19. Mid-cruise checkpoint — instruments continue commissioning over the high-altitude legs.
Closest approach 165 km on 2024-09-04. Closest flyby to date in the BepiColombo sequence; the proximity adds substantial braking ∆v.
Closest approach 37,626 km on 2024-12-01. Penultimate Mercury flyby — the final two assists shrink the orbit to the geometry required for capture.
Final flyby on 2025-01-08. A thruster power problem found in May 2024 added 11 months to the cruise, moving orbit insertion from December 2025 to November 2026.

Planned 2026-11-21. The Mercury Transfer Module separates and the two orbiters (ESA MPO + JAXA Mio) split into their respective science orbits. MPO maps the surface geology + interior structure; Mio characterises Mercury's tenuous magnetosphere. First two-orbiter Mercury mission ever flown.
First Europe + Japan joint planetary mission; second-ever spacecraft to orbit Mercury (after Messenger)

Joint ESA / JAXA mission to Mercury, launched 2018-10-20 — named after Italian mathematician Giuseppe (Bepi) Colombo, who designed Mariner 10's multi-flyby trajectory. The 8-year cruise uses 9 gravity assists (Earth 2020, Venus 2020, Venus 2021, then six Mercury flybys 2021–2025) plus continuous ion-electric thrust from the Mercury Transfer Module to bleed off the enormous solar-gravity gradient between Earth and Mercury orbits. Mercury orbit insertion 2026-11-21; science operations begin early 2027 after MTM jettison and separation of the two orbiters — ESA's MPO (planetary surface + composition) and JAXA's Mio (magnetosphere). Tests of general relativity via radio-science range tracking through Mercury's strong solar-gravity environment are also planned.
Ariane 5 ECA lifts BepiColombo from Kourou on its 8-year ion-cruise to Mercury.
Single Earth gravity assist begins the inner-system gravity-assist chain.
Second Venus gravity assist begins the Mercury approach phase.
First of six Mercury gravity assists.
MTM jettison + orbiter separation; science operations begin early 2027.
